name: economy-full-loop
description: Full economy pipeline: blast spawns fragments without instant payout, a debris_hauler hauls them into a freight_warehouse, and contract delivery pays out only from that stored inventory (issue #456).

steps.description: #553: cash bumped from $80,000 to $250,000 -- drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action, so this file needs a driller/drill_rig it never used to, and (see below) a rock_fragmenter/second driver to clear the oversized fragments this same charge always produced, on top of the original driver/debris_hauler/freight_warehouse shopping list.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts); this only raises the level for the scenario's needs -- the player-facing path is `employee train`.

expect.note: the seismic survey cost ($3000, SURVEY_COSTS.seismic) is charged up front when queued, not on completion -- Finding #32: this used to silently diverge state.finances.cash from the flat cash field this assertion reads, fixed at the root

steps.description: Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered -- a DOM-only probe silently missed events on a no-GPU runner where a frame costs ~6s, leaving them pending so later ticks halted and the run diverged while still passing command mode.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts); this only raises the level for the scenario's needs -- the player-facing path is `employee train`.

#553: drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action -- a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole -- so this file (which pre-#553 never needed a drill_rig at all) now needs one before drill_plan can ever land. Vehicle #1; destroyed by the blast further down, so the debris_hauler purchased later becomes #2 and the rock_fragmenter #3.

Grants the driller (employee #2) the licence to drive the drill_rig just purchased -- the real path is training at a driving_center (see employee-training.json's own conversion of that exact flow); left as a test-only bootstrap since this file's focus is the economy loop, not re-proving vehicle licensing.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:3 depth:6 start:10,10 diameter:0.089
steps.description: depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. This file's own expect blocks only assert hole/charge/sequence counts around the affected blast (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction -- verified both modes still pass unchanged. #553: drill_plan now only orders holes -- holeCount stays 0 until the driller actually drives the drill_rig to each one and drills it, proven by the wait step below. spacing corrected from 4 to 3 (same Finding #42 class as the depth fix just above, found while chasing issue #553's diameter mismatch): this step never clicks the grid tool's spacing stepper either, so the real drag always used the panel's own DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3 (Drill.ts) -- the declared spacing:4 was never what the real click sent, and with rows/cols landing the same 2x2 either way (round(4/3)+1 == round(4/4)+1 == 2), it only silently shifted where the 4 holes actually sit, not how many -- a small amount of extra/less driller travel between real hole positions that the diameter fix alone didn't account for. diameter:0.089 added (issue #553 shared-mechanism finding, same root cause as rock-fragmenter-breaking.json/hauling-gate.json/nav-*-visual.json): the real grid-tool confirm always sends the panel's own DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M=0.089 (Drill.ts), while an omitted diameter: on this console command fell back to a different console-only default (0.15, mining.ts) -- computeDrillHoleDurationTicks scales drill duration by diameter, so the omission alone kept the drill_rig busy (and paying fuelCostPerTick) for extra ticks in command mode that the real click's grid never spent.
#553: waits for the driller to drive the drill_rig to all 4 ordered holes and drill them -- a single 50-tick round lands the whole 2x2 grid on tutorial_pit's small map.

Defensive: a `tick N` step silently completes fewer ticks than requested if a random event fires mid-wait, and every subsequent tick then refuses until the event is resolved. No-op when nothing is pending.

role: player (issue #515): the Charge step's amount/stemming steppers and product-card explosive selector are real controls — this reaches the declared explosive/amount/stemming via clicks instead of Charge All using whatever the panel's fields already showed.
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

role: player: explicit [data-step="3"] click before Sequence controls -- relying on the panel's own autoAdvance to have already landed there is unreliable in a real interaction-mode run (element present but zero-size, i.e. a hidden inactive tab), same finding as level1-win-efficient.json/level1-playthrough-win.json/tutorial-playthrough.json.

#553: qualificationCount/proficiencyTotal bumped by 1 each over the pre-#553 baseline -- the driller (employee #2) now also carries the driving.drill_rig licence added above. #592: qualificationCount/proficiencyTotal dropped from 4/12 to 2/6 -- the blast a few steps above kills the driller (employee #2, holding blasting:5 + driving.drill_rig:1 -- confirmed via direct trace: `alive:false` on employee #2 immediately after the `blast` step), and qualificationCount/proficiencyTotal are now computed over living employees only (issue #592 -- a dead employee's frozen qualifications used to permanently pollute this aggregate). Only the surveyor (geology:5) is alive going into this hire, so 5 + this new driver's own driving.truck:1 = 6.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts); this only raises the level for the scenario's needs -- the player-facing path is `employee train`. #592: proficiencyTotal dropped from 16 to 10 -- same living-employees-only computation as the hire step just above (6 + this level bump from 1 to 5, i.e. +4, = 10); the dead driller's frozen qualifications no longer count.

#553: this file's charge (amount:3kg boomite at spacing:4) always left some oversized boulders alongside the haulable rubble -- pre-#553, blast landed at tick 0 so the single debris_hauler driver's cost-ranked action window (ACTION_SELECTION_MAX_PATH_ATTEMPTS=5, ActionSelection.ts) never filled with fragment_debris the driver could never claim (no rock_fragmenter existed). Post-#553 the drilling wait shifts nothing about the blast's own geometry, but empirically the closest 5 pending actions to a debris_hauler driver's hire position are fragment_debris, and with no rock_fragmenter ever able to claim them they never clear -- permanently starving the driver's own haul_debris candidates out of its bounded top-5 window. A second driver crewing a rock_fragmenter (bought below, before the debris_hauler) clears that oversized boulder backlog so the debris_hauler's window actually reaches a haul_debris action. Employee #4. #592: qualificationCount/proficiencyTotal dropped from 5/17 to 3/11 -- same living-employees-only computation as the two steps above (the dead driller's blasting:5 + driving.drill_rig:1 still excluded): 2 living quals (surveyor geology:5, driver#3 driving.truck:5 -- profTotal 10) + this new driver's own driving.truck:1 = 3 quals / 11 proficiency.

Unlike the driving.truck bootstrap above, this one grants a licence from nothing: employee #4 was hired as a driver (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION driving.truck only), and driving.excavator (the rock_fragmenter's licence) belongs to no hiring role at all -- the real path is training at a driving_center (see employee-training.json's own conversion of that exact flow, and rock-fragmenter-breaking.json's identical bootstrap). Left as a test-only bootstrap since this file's focus is the hauling/contract loop, not re-proving excavator licensing. #592: proficiencyTotal dropped from 22 to 16 -- same living-employees-only computation as the steps above; this adds a brand-new qualification (11 + 5 = 16) rather than raising an existing one.

#553: vehicle #2 -- #1 was the drill_rig purchased above, destroyed by the blast. Bought (and crewed, below) before the debris_hauler on purpose: newly purchased vehicles spawn staggered off the grid centre (VehicleCommands.ts), which on tutorial_pit's small map lands right in the single-file approach to the blast crater -- an idle vehicle parked there blocks any other vehicle needing the same cell (two vehicles never share one, EntityMovementTick.ts's isCellOccupiedByOtherVehicle). Buying and crewing the rock_fragmenter first, then waiting for it to actually depart its spawn tile before the debris_hauler ever exists, means neither vehicle is ever parked in the other's way.
#553: lets the rock_fragmenter's driver board and drive off toward its first boulder, clearing its spawn tile before the debris_hauler purchase below ever lands a vehicle there.

#553: vehicle #3 -- #1 was the drill_rig (destroyed by the blast), #2 the rock_fragmenter bought above. No toolbar re-click here (unlike the rock_fragmenter buy above): the Vehicles panel toggles closed on a repeat click of its own already-active toolbar button (UIManager.togglePanel, `this.activePanel === name` branch) -- it's still open from that same purchase, with only a non-UI `tick 5` and an in-panel `vehicle driver 2 4` assign-button click in between, neither of which touches the toolbar. Re-clicking it here closed the panel instead of leaving it open, so the very next click (on the still-present-but-hidden debris_hauler tier button) failed with a real, reproducible "element has zero size (0x0)" in interaction mode -- the same toggle-button class of bug as the one tracked separately for blast-visual-full.json's vehicle panel.
Long enough for the surveyor to reach (12,12) and complete the seismic survey queued at the very start.

#552: replaces the old manual 'vehicle haul 1 fragment:138' step and its .bs-vehicle-haul-btn click -- once the debris_hauler and its licensed driver exist, the on-ground fragment's own haul_debris PendingAction is claimed and driven to automatically, with no player command or button naming which fragment. Ordering a haul costs nothing, but this extra tick still drains its own tick's worth of salary/maintenance upkeep, so cash only decreases here rather than holding at the retired command's old exact equals:29770 (which itself never cost anything, only the tick around it did). The following tick-10 rounds let the drive-load-deliver cycle actually finish.

#553: the debris_hauler driver's own cost-ranked action window only starts reaching a haul_debris candidate once the rock_fragmenter has cleared enough of the oversized boulders closer to the crater -- five rounds of tick 10 (with a defensive event-resolve after each, same pattern as the drill-plan wait above) cover that, ending on the round that actually lands storedMassKg > 0.

Long enough for the rock_fragmenter to clear the boulders blocking the debris_hauler driver's own action window, and for the driver to then haul the first cleared fragment all the way to the freight_warehouse. #611: widened from tick 10 to tick 20 -- selectBestActionForEmployee's isClaimable pre-filter (issue #611) now applies over the whole candidate pool before ranking rather than only inside the bounded top-N reachability window, so an employee licensed for both vehicle roles in this file (driver #4, driving.truck + driving.excavator) reaches and reserves-ahead a haul_debris action for the debris_hauler (vehicle #3) sooner, then keeps working its own rock_fragmenter queue for longer before finally freeing up to drive the haul itself -- first pickup now lands around tick 169 (measured via direct trace) instead of within the original tick-10 round ending at 167, a couple of ticks too early to observe. 20 ticks reaches tick 177, well past the first delivery.

#554-followup (issue #586 CI): the accept step below waits on a specific *type* of offer (rubble_disposal, 30% of generated contracts, Contract.ts's generateOneContract) being present in the pool at the moment of the click, not a fixed id -- but the pool only regenerates every REFRESH_INTERVAL=20 ticks (Contract.ts), and interaction mode's own real-clock tick pacing (no GPU, ~6s/frame, #475) advances the game far slower in real time than command mode's tick-driven loop, so a static `waitForSelector` at its 10s default timeout could easily expire inside a single lull between refreshes, or catch a refresh whose 3 fresh slots (CONTRACTS_PER_REFRESH) happened not to roll rubble_disposal. Speeding up time here (matching the charge/sequence steps' own `time speed 8`/`time speed 1` convention elsewhere in this file) and widening the wait's own timeout below buys enough real-time-to-game-tick throughput to cover several refresh cycles instead of a fraction of one, so the wait resolves on the pool's own eventual regeneration rather than racing a single snapshot of it.

#513/#581: the accept click is scoped to `[data-contract-id]`, the contract this step's `command` names (ContractsPanel sets `data-contract-id` on offered cards via `makeOfferedCard`), so command mode and interaction mode are guaranteed to accept the same contract instead of command mode taking the named id literally while an unscoped click took whatever led the DOM. #553-followup (issue #586 CI): a genuine duplicate JSON `description` key on this step silently discarded a first, correct description ('contract ID drifted from #1 to #6 -- CONTRACT_REFRESH_INTERVAL keeps rolling the counter forward while this file's own drilling/hauling wait grew by well over a hundred ticks') and kept only this second, boilerplate one -- which still pointed the interaction selectors at the stale id 1 even though the command itself had already been updated to 6. Fixed both scoped selectors to match. #554: `contract accept 6` -> `contract accept type:rubble_disposal` -- charging is real work too now, and the extra ticks the charge-order waits above spend shift the tick-based contract pool refresh far enough that a fixed id is no longer a reliable bet at all; `type:`/`material:` selectors (ContractSelector, #597) name a contract by what it actually is rather than where it landed in generation order. This file only ever accepts one contract, so `type:rubble_disposal` is unambiguous both in `available` at accept time and in `active` at deliver time below -- no `[data-contract-id]` scoping is needed to disambiguate multiple same-type offers the way core-loop-visual.json's guard steps do. #554-followup (issue #586 CI): a widened 90s `waitForSelector` timeout (and a matching 100s step-level `timeout` so the harness's own step budget doesn't cut it off first) plus `time speed 8` beforehand (the step above) replace a bare 10s wait against a single pool snapshot -- see that step's own description for why the type-scoped selector alone wasn't enough. `time speed 1` restored in a separate setup step below -- role:player's own interaction array may never contain a `command` action (`checkStepActionAllowed`), so the restore can't live inside this step.
Restore normal speed after the widened contract-accept wait above.

Real click path: type 200 into the ACTIVE card's amount box and press DELIVER, so the kilograms the click sends are the same 200 the `command` field declares. The panel is already open from the accept step above, and contract #6 is the only active card, so the unqualified `.bs-contract-amount`/`.bs-contract-deliver` selectors are unambiguous here. awaitUsable is the real assertion: ContractsPanel disables the input, MAX and DELIVER together whenever min(remaining, stored) is 0, so a run that hauled nothing fails here instead of quietly delivering nothing. #553: contract #6 ("Dispose of rubble", 330kg @ $1.95/kg) needs 330kg total against the ~1050kg the hauling waits above have already stored, so 200 is genuinely deliverable.

expect.note: #553: delivery genuinely pays out here (unlike contract-negotiation.json, which never hauls anything into storage) -- confirmed via direct trace against contract #6's $1.95/kg rubble rate.

steps.description: #553: employeeCount/vehicleCount bumped over the pre-#553 baseline -- employee #2 (the driller, needed to drive the drill_rig) and employee #4 (the second driver, crewing the rock_fragmenter) are both new. vehicleCount is 2: the debris_hauler and rock_fragmenter are both still alive; the drill_rig (#1) was destroyed by the blast and no longer counts.
